title: D-FINE vs RF-DETR: 61.4 vs 58.6 mAP at the top end
dek: D-FINE averages 7.5 mAP points more than RF-DETR at matched size and wins both pairs. RF-DETR runs 35.8% faster on an RTX 5070 Ti.
author: Vision Analysis

blocks.text: D-FINE is the more accurate family: at matched parameter counts on an RTX 5070 Ti it averages 7.5 mAP points higher than RF-DETR and wins both nearest-params pairings. It also holds the top: D-FINE-X reaches 61.4 mAP against RF-DETR-L at 58.6. The trade is speed: RF-DETR runs 35.8% faster on average in PyTorch. Pick D-FINE for accuracy and RF-DETR for throughput.

D-FINE fields 5 measured variants and RF-DETR fields 4, all on the same COCO val2017 protocol on an RTX 5070 Ti. RF-DETR's variants sit between 30.47M and 33.93M parameters, so only 2 pairings match closely by parameter count: D-FINE-M and D-FINE-L, both against RF-DETR-N.

blocks.caption: Accuracy vs parameters on COCO val2017, D-FINE and RF-DETR variants highlighted against the full field.

blocks.text: mAP is shown in percent. The comparison pairs each D-FINE variant with the nearest RF-DETR variant by parameter count. D-FINE-M (19.59M) beats RF-DETR-N by 6.4 points and D-FINE-L (31.24M) by 8.6, for a mean of 7.5. At the top end D-FINE-X reaches 61.4 mAP against RF-DETR-L at 58.6. At the small end D-FINE-N is a 3.78M model at 45.8 mAP, far lighter than RF-DETR's smallest at 30.47M and 51.4 mAP.
Averaged across the matched pairs, RF-DETR is 35.8% faster than D-FINE in PyTorch. RF-DETR-N runs 39.5 FPS against 28.8 for D-FINE-M and 21.9 for D-FINE-L.

Pick D-FINE when you want the most accuracy per parameter: it leads at both matched sizes and reaches 61.4 mAP at the top. Pick RF-DETR when throughput is the constraint, since it runs 35.8% faster on average in this pairing. Both ship under Apache-2.0, so licensing does not force the call.
